teaching.hint: For a substring, which information about each letter matters: its full count or only part of that count?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Substring parity is the XOR difference of two prefix-parity masks; wonderful substrings correspond to equal masks or masks differing in one bit.
solution_outline.approach: Scan the word, toggling one of ten parity bits. Before recording the current prefix, add frequencies of earlier prefixes with the same mask or each one-bit neighbor, then increment its frequency.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The frequency table contains exactly earlier prefix masks. Their XOR with the current mask describes each substring ending now.
solution_outline.correctness: A mask difference of zero has all even counts; one set bit has exactly one odd-count letter. Every earlier prefix makes one unique substring ending at the current position, and every wonderful one appears in one queried category.
solution_outline.pitfall: The empty prefix must be counted before scanning so substrings starting at the first character are included.

common_wrong_turns: Counting distinct substring texts instead of occurrences
source_fidelity_notes: Removed verbose examples; retained nonempty occurrence counting, ten-letter alphabet, and wide result.
